title: Vendor-neutral DDIL test and conformance harness for tactical software (link emulation, multi-node TAK/CoT sync scoring, pre-Jailbreak API contract tests, TAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance)

scores.rationale: Real but episodic: Operation Jailbreak needed ~600 people from 55-80 firms to expose interfaces (DefenseScoop 2026-05-29, FACT/HIGH); Ivy Sting 4-5 found DDIL and code faults live with industry 'fixing the code in almost real time' (DVIDS 2026-03-30, FACT/HIGH); the Sept 2025 AO memo made missing RBAC/audit an authorization blocker (CNBC 2025-10-03, RECALL/MEDIUM). But the pain is absorbed by exercise time and engineer hours, not by lost missions, and the government has already stood up labs (Radio Rodeo, ATEC/SIL hardening) to reduce it.

Integration events now recur on a monthly-to-quarterly cadence (Ivy Sting iterations, Jailbreak series incl. Falcon Fury, NetModX persistent experimentation) so the vendor population feels it repeatedly, but any single vendor faces a pre-sprint deadline only a few times a year.

Explained 1: no budget line, RFI, OTA or task order for a neutral test/conformance harness was found. The only solicited demand is Army SBIR A254-019 (Phase I up to $250k, 2025-02, FACT/HIGH), routed through xTechIgnite to Assured Information Security's GRUNTS (xtech.army.mil 2025-05, FACT/MEDIUM), i.e. already assigned and Phase I-scale. NGC2's ~$3.78B FY27 request (Breaking Defense 2026-04) and 50% obligation cap (FNN 2026-02) fund primes and government labs, not test tooling; government T&E is institutionally funded inside C5ISR Center and ATEC. Not 0 because A254-019 proves the Army will spend at least Phase I money on DDIL test tooling.

Vendor B2B sales need no vehicle but are tiny; the government route runs through xTech/SBIR (ownership-gated for this team, 13 CFR 121.702) or an unsolicited C5ISR Center / prime T&E task order with no precedent found; NetModX and xTech hackathons offer access to users but not purchase orders.

Explained 5: every component exists as open or public software - ATAK-CIV and TAK Server (government open source), NRL EMANE/CORE and Linux netem for link emulation, public Lattice SDK schemas and free Sandboxes, standard contract-test and SBOM/OSCAL tooling. Building a scenario runner and scorer on top is engineering, not research.

Explained 5: proof of concept estimated at $40-90k and a credible lab demo at $150-400k (HYPOTHESIS), well inside $250k for the first two stages; no hardware beyond ~10 SBCs/laptops or cloud containers; no ATO or classified access needed.

A scored multi-node TAK DDIL run and a plugin conformance report are achievable in 3-4 months; 'credible military demo' still requires an event slot (NetModX, Radio Rodeo, Jailbreak-series) whose timing the founders do not control.

Synthetic CoT/MAVLink traffic, public TAK and Lattice schemas and DARPA FLUID's published 1 Mbps-1 kbps regime cover the MVP; real PoR radio traces, SRW/WNW EMANE waveform models and exercise captures are controlled and unobtainable without a sponsor, which caps realism.

Open-core software on public inputs carries low export-control and no ATO burden; deductions for SBIR ownership rules (13 CFR 121.702, FACT/HIGH), AFWERX foreign-national limits (2025-07-02, FACT/HIGH) and the need for a technology control plan if any controlled inputs are touched. Counsel required; no legal determination.

Explained 5: the entire product is unclassified by construction - ATAK-CIV is open source, TAK.gov's third-party pipeline is open to anyone not on the Denied Parties List, Lattice Sandboxes are free and public, EMANE/CORE are public; classification only enters if a government lab later feeds it controlled traces.

Each layer is occupied: government labs (C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo 2026-03/04, ATEC and APG/Huntsville SILs), free government-sponsored emulators (NRL EMANE/CORE with SRW/WNW ports), commercial emulators (Keysight EXata/JNE, Apposite, iTrinegy), platform sandboxes (Anduril Lattice Sandboxes, free), TAK Server's own takcl test framework, and the xTechIgnite winner AIS GRUNTS for the GenAI DDIL simulation ask. Only the cross-vendor scoring layer is unoccupied, and absence of a competitor there is not evidence of demand.

Explained 1: the parties that would have to buy or bless a neutral harness (Army CTO/AO, C5ISR Center, ATEC, TAK Product Center, NGC2 team leads) already own the acceptance authority and run their own labs, and the platform owners give the API-side test environment away for free to grow their ecosystems; none is exposed by, or needs, an outside scorer.

TAK/CoT and the TAK Server Mission API are open and documented; Lattice SDK schemas are public with free sandboxes; Ditto SDK is licensable commercially; the closed parts (PoR radio management planes, CUI ICDs) can be excluded from the harness without breaking the core value.

Explained 1: scenario libraries and scoring rubrics are replicable in weeks by Anduril, Ditto, TAK Product Center or a government lab; there is no owned data, interface, accreditation or credential gate; the only durable asset would be a government designation of the report as accepted evidence, for which no signal exists.

Offline-first and network-partition testing has commercial analogues (public safety apps, maritime, mining, retail edge), but generic chaos-engineering and WAN-emulation tools already serve them and the TAK/AO-specific modules have no commercial pull.

Could extend to Ditto/Lattice adapters, allied TAK users (NATO, Bundeswehr D-LBO ecosystem) and T&E services, but every extension stays inside a lab-tool and services niche whose ceiling is well below venture scale.

Per-sprint readiness engagements and lab licences recur, but at low price points ($5-25k per engagement, INFERENCE) from a vendor base of ~50-80 firms per event, and government labs would more likely adopt an open-source bench than pay per run.

The strong engineer can build the whole bench on public code, and the non-U.S.-person founder is not blocked from the open-core work (INFERENCE; counsel to confirm); the business founder can sell readiness runs to vendors. Missing: any tactical-network T&E credibility, operator or lab relationships, and an SBIR-eligible cap table - the first is rated fatal if not recruited.

market.summary: No requirement owner, program office, contracting office, budget line or vehicle exists for a neutral harness; the government performs test and conformance itself (C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo, NetModX, ATEC and APG/Huntsville SILs), the one solicited DDIL test-tooling ask was a $250k Phase I already routed to AIS via xTechIgnite, and the residual vendor market is episodic and low-price, so the business drifts into consultancy.

competition.summary: Every layer already has a free or entrenched supplier - NRL EMANE/CORE, Keysight/Apposite, Anduril's free Lattice Sandboxes, TAK Server's takcl framework and signing pipeline - and the platform owners or labs can publish their own DDIL benchmark in weeks; the startup's only differentiator, impartiality, matters only if a government body designates its report, which nothing evidences.

feasibility.summary: This lens does not kill the gap: the harness is fully unclassified, buildable on public code for well under $250k, and the non-U.S.-person founder can work on the open core; the constraints (SBIR ownership, controlled waveform models and radio traces, lack of T&E credibility) limit growth and realism, not the ability to build and demonstrate.

verdict_rationale: KILL as a venture; keep as a sub-$60k open-source credibility asset. Applying the chain test: PROBLEM (real, FACT/HIGH) -> USER (vendor, prime and lab T&E engineers, FACT) -> REQUIREMENT OWNER: the DDIL-resilience and interface-conformance requirements are owned by CPE C2IN, the Army CTO/AO and ADOC, who have chosen to satisfy them through government labs (C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo 2026-03/04; ATEC and APG/Huntsville SIL hardening of 74+ jailbroken capabilities; Army Software Factory validation) and prime T&E -> PROGRAM OFFICE: none for test tooling -> CONTRACTING OFFICE: none identified (Public evidence insufficient) -> BUDGET: no line; the only solicited money is Army SBIR A254-019 (Phase I up to $250k) already routed through xTechIgnite to Assured Information Security's GRUNTS -> VEHICLE: BREAK, and the one open rail (SBIR) is ownership-gated for this team. The major penalty applies. Two independently sufficient kill reasons: (1) the function is government-owned and already resourced, on top of free government-sponsored emulators (NRL EMANE/CORE) and free platform sandboxes (Anduril Lattice Sandboxes), so a neutral harness has no buyer who needs it; (2) the residual buyer set (50-80 small vendors per sprint) is an episodic, low-price services market with a replicable product and no moat. Market attractiveness 2.4 (budget 1, incumbent vulnerability 1, moat 1); founder fit 4.2 is high precisely because the thing is cheap, open and legal to build - which is also why it is not a company. Confidence HIGH on the venture-scale question; MEDIUM on individual facts drawn from search summaries (AIS GRUNTS selection, ATEC article details) and RECALL items from parent cards.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline - killed as a venture. The residual, survivable form is explicitly not a company: an open-source 'TAK DDIL bench' (netem/EMANE link profiles, ~10 ATAK-CIV/TAK Server nodes, sync-scoring report) plus an ATAK plugin RBAC/audit/SBOM conformance module, released publicly and used (a) to sell a handful of fixed-fee pre-sprint readiness runs to Jailbreak-series vendors, (b) as the entry into a NetModX / C5ISR Center persistent-experimentation slot or xTech hackathon, and (c) as the credibility asset that gets the founders into an NGC2 sub-vendor, a prime T&E cell or a TAK plugin shop. Size it at $30-60k and 3-4 months, expect no government purchase, and treat any lab adoption as a relationship, not revenue.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders with $250,000 insisted on this gap, they should spend no more than $30-60k and four months building the open-source TAK DDIL bench: containerised ATAK-CIV and TAK Server nodes behind netem or EMANE/CORE profiles spanning 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted 30-minute partitions and reconnect storms, a scorer reporting time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicates and conflicts after reconnect and link saturation, a CoT/TAK Mission API and public-Lattice-schema contract-test CLI, and an ATAK plugin module that emits an RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage and SBOM as a signed OSCAL-style bundle. They would show it to three or four small vendors facing the next Jailbreak-series date (MatrixSpace/Adyton-class), a C5ISR Center tactical-network S&T lead through a NetModX or Radio Rodeo application, and a Team Anduril or Team Lockheed T&E engineer. The demo would prove that a reproducible score exposes, before the event, the failures (arrival order, duplicate tracks after reconnect, saturation, missing audit events) that today are discovered live at Ivy Sting and Jailbreak, and the vendor would care because failing at the sprint costs a fielding window while the lab would care because comparable numbers help it triage 50-80 vendors. An incumbent cannot be bothered to crush it - Anduril already gives away Lattice Sandboxes, TAK Product Center ships its own test framework, and C5ISR Center and ATEC run the labs - which is exactly the problem: nobody needs to buy it, and any of them can publish an equivalent benchmark in weeks if it ever mattered. The only milestone that would justify $2-5M is an external designation - a C5ISR Center, Army CTO/AO or TAK Product Center statement that the bench's report is accepted pre-event or acceptance evidence, backed by a task order or Phase II-scale award and a prime subcontract to run it - and no public evidence suggests that event is coming inside the founders' runway; the one solicited dollar for DDIL test tooling already went to an established SBIR firm. So it fails as a company: build it small, publish it, use it to earn relationships and a first subcontract, and put the venture-scale ambition and the $250k elsewhere.
bear_case_summary: Test and conformance of tactical software is a government-owned function the Army is resourcing itself: C5ISR Center's laboratory DDIL effects (Radio Rodeo, March-April 2026, FACT/HIGH), NetModX persistent experimentation (FACT/HIGH), ATEC-supported hardening of 74+ jailbroken capabilities at Huntsville and APG SILs (FACT/MEDIUM) and Army Software Factory validation of jailbroken interfaces (RECALL/MEDIUM). The emulation layer is free government software (NRL EMANE/CORE, FACT/HIGH) or a mature commercial appliance market (Keysight, Apposite), the API-side test environment is free from the platform owner (Lattice Sandboxes, FACT/HIGH), TAK signing is free and government-run, and the only solicited DDIL test-tooling money (A254-019, Phase I up to $250k) is already routed to AIS via xTechIgnite (FACT/MEDIUM). There is no requirement owner, program office, budget line or vehicle for a neutral harness; SBIR is ownership-gated for this cap table (13 CFR 121.702, FACT/HIGH); the residual market is 50-80 small vendors buying episodic readiness runs, which is a consultancy. Confidence HIGH.
bull_case_summary: The pain is real and now has dates: Jailbreak is a series (Fort Carson May 2026, Falcon Fury), Ivy Sting iterates monthly, NGC2 must scale across divisions and corps, the common data baseline (2026-06), API Marketplace (2026-05) and public Lattice schemas make conformance testable, DARPA FLUID and A254-019 define the DDIL regime, and the Sept 2025 AO memo made RBAC/audit evidence an authorization gate. The MVP is unusually accessible - unclassified, open-source-buildable for tens of thousands of dollars, legal for the non-U.S.-person founder to build (INFERENCE; counsel to confirm), and exportable to allied TAK users. If a C5ISR Center lab, TAK Product Center or an NGC2 team lead adopted a neutral bench as its pre-event gate, the first mover would hold a small, recurring, mandated niche across NGC2, TAK and allied TAK ecosystems. This is a credible open-source project and services wedge, and a plausible acqui-hire, not a venture-scale company; the adoption event it depends on is unevidenced (HYPOTHESIS/LOW).
